subjects.displayTitle: Women’s roles: education, courage, and the common good
subjects.introduction: Humanity, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches, is a bird with two wings, and no nation rises beyond the point its women have reached. The vision this opens is practical. Girls must be schooled, because the mother is the child’s first teacher and what she lacks all humankind lacks; women must press into science, literature and history, speak in public, study the proofs of their faith, and gather to learn how to teach. Tahirih, a scholar from the clerical class who faced down Shah and clergy, shows what such courage looks like, and Mary Magdalene, who steadied the shaken disciples, shows that it is ancient. Some of this is spoken in the idiom of its day, counting believing women among men and heroes, and the harsh words once used for women in the East are recalled only to mark how far grace has carried them. Priscilla and Aquila, taking an eloquent preacher aside to teach him more fully, offer a quiet parallel: a community is measured by whose insight it can recognise. The way forward runs through the equality of women and men, the education and moral training of children, and the prayers written for women who are asked to carry so much.
subjects.arc: Begin with humanity’s shared progress, establish equality and education, follow women into teaching and public life, consider historical language and constraints, then return to courage, compassion, and enduring service.

order.why: Open with the shared consequences of restricting either wing of humanity.
Give advancement a concrete scope in science, literature, and history.
shortened: Women must go on advancing; they must extend their knowledge of science, literature, history, for the perfection of humanity.

order.why: Establish equal reception of divine bestowals.
shortened: In this great Cycle and wondrous Dispensation some women have been raised up who were the emblems of unity and ensigns of oneness, for the revelation of divine bestowals is received by men and women in equal measure. "Verily the most honoured in the sight of God is the most virtuous amongst you"5 is applicable to both men and women, to servants and handmaidens.

order.why: Read bounty as available across sex and age.
shortened: In receiving the bounties from the cloud of the Lord's mercy, men and women are equal, and "All do We aid, both these and those, and the gift of thy Lord is not limited" is established and applicable in this regard. Thus the garment of sanctification of the love of God and the blessed robe of the knowledge of God fits every stature harmoniously, whether male or female, whether old or young.

order.why: Question male superiority as a universal claim.
Keep the explicit rejection of treating all men as strong and all women as weak.
Connect a girls’ school with the advancement of the age.
shortened: Devote ye particular attention to the school for girls, for the greatness of this wondrous Age will be manifested as a result of progress in the world of women. This is why ye observe that in every land the world of women is on the march, and this is due to the impact of the Most Great Manifestation, and the power of the teachings of God.

order.why: Read the direct call for diligent education of women.
Consider progress where opportunities had been absent.
shortened: Erelong will women in every field keep pace with the men.

Until now, in Persia, the means for women's advancement were non-existent. But now, God be thanked, ever since the dawning of the Morn of Salvation, they have been going forward day by day. The hope is that they will take the lead in virtues and attainments, in closeness to the Court of Almighty God, in faith and certitude--and that the women of the East will become the envy of the women of the West.

order.why: Read the reported change from exclusion from literacy toward girls’ schools.
Join education, early nurture, scholarship, and public ability.
shortened: Furthermore, the education of woman is more necessary and important than that of man, for woman is the trainer of the child from its infancy. If she be defective and imperfect herself, the child will necessarily be deficient; therefore, imperfection of woman implies a condition of imperfection in all mankind, for it is the mother who rears, nurtures and guides the growth of the child.
They are eloquent; they are poets and scholars and embody the quintessence of humility. In political ability and acumen they have been able to cope and compete with representative men.

order.why: Consider the argument for giving girls’ education particular priority.
shortened: The question of training the children and looking after the orphans is extremely important, but most important of all is the education of girl children, for these girls will one day be mothers, and the mother is the first teacher of the child. In whatever way she reareth the child, so will the child become, and the results of that first training will remain with the individual throughout his entire life, and it would be most difficult to alter them. And how can a mother, herself ignorant and untrained, educate her child? It is therefore clear that the education of girls is of far greater consequence than that of boys.

order.why: Read the formation of virtue and resilience in early life.
Hear the account of mothers as first mentors.
shortened: For mothers are the first educators, the first mentors; and truly it is the mothers who determine the happiness, the future greatness, the courteous ways and learning and judgement, the understanding and the faith of their little ones.

order.why: Consider the gardener’s care as a model of education.
shortened: Let the mothers consider that whatever concerneth the education of children is of the first importance. Let them put forth every effort in this regard, for when the bough is green and tender it will grow in whatever way ye train it. Therefore is it incumbent upon the mothers to rear their little ones even as a gardener tendeth his young plants. Let them strive by day and by night to establish within their children faith and certitude, the fear of God, the love of the Beloved of the worlds, and all good qualities and traits.

order.why: Read a mother’s knowledge, insight, and character in relation to nurture.
shortened: Consider that these girls will one day become mothers, and the life and salvation of children, their deliverance and success, depend upon and are conditioned by these mothers' good character and abundance of perfections. If a mother is perfect, knowledgeable, learned, believing and insightful, she will nurse her children at the breast of the love of God, lead them to the knowledge of God, establish sound education, and from an early age nurture the children in human perfections and virtues.

order.why: Consider education as worship and service.
Extend encouragement from one educator to other women.
shortened: O handmaiden of God! Arouse and entice the handmaidens of God, and show them the way of training the children with enthusiasm and detachment, because the first educators of children are mothers.

order.why: Keep the training of boys and girls together.
Read justice in marriage through shared physical and spiritual feelings.
shortened: I beseech God that He may bestow divine characteristics upon thy noble son Ali-Akbar and deliver him from changing wives, for this matter is contrary to God's good-pleasure and opposed to justice and fairness in the human world, since women are like men in both physical and spiritual feelings.

order.why: Join cooperative progress with the reported example of Tahirih.
shortened: Unless both eyes are normal the visual process cannot be perfect. Similarly, until man and woman attain the realization of co-equality the progress of the world will be hindered.

There have been many women in Persia who have been eloquent, courageous and long-suffering in the support of the Bahai cause. Among them was the famous Kurat-ul-Ayn, a most scholarly woman belonging to the ecclesiastical class. She proclaimed the cause of woman with unshakable courage, withstanding the oppression of the Shah of Persia and of the ulama. Finally she was martyred, but to her last breath she was eloquent and fearless in defending her faith.

order.why: Consider the value of women’s judgment in national affairs.
shortened: In all questions which concern the welfare of a nation, is not the woman's view as important as the man's, if one would get a just and true consideration of all sides of that question? Therefore I am in favour of votes for women on every subject.

order.why: Read the two wings alongside the statement of political detachment.
shortened: Regarding women's suffrage, this is a political issue and I am detached from all political matters, however I will say this much: both men and women are human and are like two wings for the world of humanity.

order.why: Keep participation in institutions and the stated Universal House of Justice exception explicit.
Read voting rights and the source’s discussion of future progress.
shortened: He says: "O ye men of the House of Justice!"

But when its members are to be elected, the right which belongs to women, so far as their voting and their voice is concerned, is indisputable. When the women attain to the ultimate degree of progress, then, according to the exigency of the time and place and their great capacity, they shall obtain extraordinary privileges.

order.why: Consider the historical counsel on women’s educational gatherings and wise action.
shortened: The individual women should, today, follow a course of action which will be the cause of eternal glory to all womankind, so that all women will be illumined. And that lieth in gathering to learn how to teach, in holding meetings to recite the verses, to offer supplications to the kingdom of the Lord of evident signs, and to institute education for the girls. Ponder the manner in which Jinab-i-Tahirih used to teach. She was free from every concern, and for this reason she was resplendent.

order.why: Read the particular teaching assembly’s mandate and its distinction from consultation.
shortened: As to the Assembly of Teaching, the revered members of which are the maid-servants of the Merciful, they are also assisted by the help and the providence of the Beauty of El-ABHA.

But all of their mention and thought in their meeting should be confined to teaching the truth, and to constantly persuade people in pure and divine brilliancy and in absolute godlike spirituality. They should not interfere with the affairs which have regard to the Board of Consultation, because confusion of thought conduces to division and causes disturbance to the mind, and then pure spirituality would cease.

order.why: Follow the encouragement to multiply gatherings for learning and teaching.
shortened: Now it is necessary that you encourage and urge that the teaching gathering for women be multiplied, and there is no doubt that this first gathering that has been formed will be the cause of establishing great gatherings.

They must be so trained that in a short time maidens and women will arise to teach the Cause of the One True God with perfect eloquence and fluency, and through the power of proof render men of all nations helpless and wanting.

order.why: Read the expectation of persuasive and eloquent speech.
shortened: This matter is very important, and when it is properly realized, such distinguished women will be trained in it that with eloquent speech and persuasive expression they will astound the world and render the eloquent ones of East and West silent and speechless. Today in the West, women have surpassed men.

order.why: Keep the companion account of public teaching and argument.
Consider study of proofs and laws as preparation to teach.
shortened: As for the matter of teaching classes, this is very appropriate. The women must certainly become informed of divine proofs and evidences and become cognizant of the laws of the Most Holy Book so they can guide other women to the Living Waters.

order.why: Read dignity in the sharing of knowledge across women and men.
shortened: Likewise, teaching the Faith to the female members of the family and other women is also very appropriate, for it is permissible for women to benefit from men in sciences and perfections and to receive truths and meanings, but with perfect dignity and all that modesty and chastity require.

order.why: Consider women’s words and writings as a lasting contribution.
shortened: O handmaid of God! The handmaids of the All-Merciful shall acquire resounding fame throughout all regions in the course of centuries and ages. Consider that Mary Magdalene spoke but a few words concerning the Cause of God, yet how these words spread and acquired great significance in the ears of the world. And now the handmaids of the All-Merciful speak with matchless utterance, and each one of them hath authored works that shall assume great importance in future ages.

order.why: Read the prediction of teaching extending throughout the world.
Hear the invitation for women in the East to manifest their capacities.
shortened: In America, the women have outdone the men in this regard and have taken the lead in this field. They strive harder in guiding the peoples of the world, and their endeavours are greater. They are confirmed by divine bestowals and blessings. It is my hope that in the East the handmaids of the Merciful will also exert such effort, reveal their powers, and manifest their capacities.

order.why: Give teaching its qualities of tenderness, friendliness, and compassion.
Read the prayer for eloquence, praise, and guidance.
Consider the vineyard and watering trees as images of service.
shortened: "Arise to serve the Cause of God in the vineyard of God and water the developed and flourishing trees with the waters of mysteries which are deposited in the innermost parts of the words of the Books; and be assured that the fountain of assurance will gush out in the hearts of the firm and steadfast women believers, and the divine graces will strengthen them from all sides, and the Lord will enable them to diffuse the fragrances.

order.why: Hear the encouragement of women’s gatherings.
shortened: Bring the handmaidens of the Merciful to attraction and ecstasy and make the women's gatherings the pride of men's assemblies.

order.why: Read the possibility of one person awakening others’ enthusiasm.
Consider the petition for attraction and spiritual renewal.
Read the prayer for a woman as a beacon of guidance.
shortened: O Lord! Make her a sign of Your gift among the handmaidens and a beacon of Your guidance shining and illuminating between earth and heaven.

order.why: Consider the Solomon and Sheba imagery in the summons to communicate glad tidings.
shortened: Ask God that you may convey the glad tidings of the true Solomon to the Sheba of the world of possibility, and give the good news of eternal spiritual sovereignty to the ears of the people of that land. Then, with an illumined face, you will shine like a candle in the gathering of the handmaids of the All-Merciful, burn away the veil of suspicions and imaginings, raise the banner of sanctification, and in the fire of the love of God melt and burn and be content.

order.why: Read self-forgetful service and clear argument together.
Explore the account of women who arose in successive religious dispensations.
shortened: O handmaids of the All-Merciful! During the dispensation of every sanctified Manifestation, a number of women were attracted and aroused from the tombs of the material world and were called to the magnificent gathering place of the spirit. They drank their fill from the chalice of the wine of guidance from the hand of the Cupbearer of grace, and received heavenly confirmations from the Revealer of the signs of divine power. Thereafter, with an eloquent speech, a sweet utterance, a fervour and enthusiasm born of God, they scattered to every corner of the world.

order.why: Read the historical examples as narrated in this address.
shortened: When we look at history, we see how many renowned women there have been, both in religion and in politics. In religion, a woman became the cause of deliverance and victories for the children of Israel.

In the Christian Dispensation it was Mary Magdalene who was the cause of the steadfastness of the disciples. After Jesus all the disciples were shaken, but Mary Magdalene, like unto a lion, remained firm.
In the time of Muhammad, there were two women who were more learned than other women and became promoters of the Islamic Faith. Thus it became clear that women also have their luminaries.

order.why: Consider its education argument, historical narratives, and call to work for peace.
shortened: In the Cause of Baha'u'llah there have been women who were superior to men in illumination, intellect, divine virtues and devotion to God. Among them was Qurratu'l-'Ayn.

Therefore, strive to show in the human world that women are most capable and efficient, that their hearts are more tender and susceptible than the hearts of men, that they are more philanthropic and responsive toward the needy and suffering, that they are inflexibly opposed to war and are lovers of peace. Strive that the ideal of international peace may become realized through the efforts of womankind, for man is more inclined to war than woman, and a real evidence of woman's superiority will be her service and efficiency in the establishment of universal peace.

order.why: Keep the reported comparisons of strength and governing ability in their historical form.
shortened: Abdu'l-Baha then continued more seriously: "The woman is indeed of the greater importance to the race. She has the greater burden and the greater work.

"The mere size of the brain has been proved to be no measure of superiority. The woman has greater moral courage than the man; she has also special gifts which enable her to govern in moments of danger and crisis. If necessary she can become a warrior."

order.why: Read the account of women’s learning and judgment in Islamic history.
Keep the particular assessment of Tahirih and American women attributed to its report.
Consider a gathering and its building as evidence of advancement.
Read the reported expectation of women’s part in civilization.
Consider the account of spiritual power gaining over bodily force.
Read the reported pillars supporting the arch of life.
Hear the concise charge to work for women’s emancipation.
Consider the reported counsel to pursue rights through educational means.
Read the particular criticism of methods in its historical suffrage setting.
Consider release from inherited traditions through investigation.
Read the account of degrading expressions as a critique of their use.
shortened: In this wondrous Dispensation, the handmaidens of the All-Merciful must offer a thousand thanks at every moment that the hand of grace has delivered women from the depths of abasement and raised them to the summit of men's glory. Consider what a bounty this is, for the group of women had fallen to such a degree in the East that when mention was made of women in the Arabic language, one would say "Far be it from thee" just as one would say "Far be it from thee to be a donkey."
Now, praise be to God, under the shadow of the Blessed One's grace, women are held in the utmost respect.

order.why: Keep the reported contrast between former insults and spiritual accomplishment.
shortened: Women in Persia were treated badly in former times by the Muhammadans. When speaking evil of a man, they would say, 'He is just like a woman.' When they wished to lower a man's pride, they would say, 'He is a woman, not a man.'

In this Day see what great firmness and strength women are showing for God. The way to spiritual attainment in this Dispensation will be made more and more easy for women, for they are more devoted and zealous in this Cause than men. How many women are higher than men in moral and spiritual development!

order.why: Read this broad historical characterization as the source’s account.
shortened: Formerly in India, Persia and throughout the Orient, she was not considered a human being.
The worst insult one could hurl at a man was to cry out, "Thou woman!"
From the moment Baha'u'llah appeared, this changed. He did away with the idea of distinction between the sexes, proclaiming them equal in every capacity.

order.why: Keep the companion historical characterization attributed to its report.
shortened: From the lowest degree of humiliation He hath uplifted her to the highest realm of heavenly brightness.

In Persia, Arabia, India, Turkey and other Asiatic countries woman was a negligible personality, a creature not to be trusted - belonging to the lower order of creation. One of the most opprobrious insults that could be heaped upon a man of some spirits was to call him a "woman."

order.why: Read the comparison of educational attainments as a particular reported judgment.
Consider the contrast drawn between household life and teaching in its historical setting.
Distinguish outward veiling from the source’s judgment about chastity.
Read the counsel on purity and veiling with its source omission retained.
shortened: In the divine texts it is written, and the meaning of the verse in Persian is that even if the most beautiful women were to pass before them, their gaze would never turn in that direction.

The assured and tranquil believing women must become renowned throughout all regions for their complete purity, sanctity, chastity, virtue, modesty, veiling, and bashfulness, so that all may testify to their purity, cleanliness, and virtuous qualities.

order.why: Consider the constellation of devotional, family, and personal qualities named here.
shortened: Of a surety, there is no greater pride and glory for a woman than to be a handmaid in God's Court of Grandeur; and the qualities that shall merit her this station are an alert and wakeful heart; a firm conviction of the unity of God, the Peerless; a heartfelt love for all His maidservants; spotless purity and chastity; obedience to and consideration for her husband; attention to the education and nurturing of her children; composure, calmness, dignity and self-possession; diligence in praising God, and worshipping Him both night and day; constancy and firmness in His holy Covenant; and the utmost ardour, enthusiasm, and attachment to His Cause.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s distinct prescriptions and their emphasis on kindness and honor.
shortened: God hath ordained that ye should be kind to women, honor them and revere them, that ye may be merciful.

There is no blame on them in prayer if their hair should emerge from their veils - this is God's grace and mercy upon them, that they may give thanks unto God Who created them, and that ye too may be thankful.

order.why: Read the reported explanation of inclusive masculine language.
Consider how the text relocates manliness from appearance to qualities.
Read the explicit explanation of masculine and feminine language as metaphor.
shortened: O dust at the threshold of grandeur! Masculinity and femininity pertain to the soul, not to the body - to the heart, not to clay. For these two physical attributes are metaphorical, while their spiritual reality is truth. For we observe that a male person with an elephant-like physique can be as lowly, contemptible and weak as an ant, while behind the veil of chastity and purity, a female can be the epitome of strength and power - the former enslaved by self and passion, the latter noble through reason and restraint; the former sinful and the latter virtuous.

order.why: Keep the summons to courage in its historical idiom.
shortened: O handmaidens, arise with manly courage to serve the Cause of God! Many women are today remembered before God as being superior to men, and some men who are counted as women.

order.why: Read heroism through the source’s gendered language.
Consider the sharp figurative reversal of expected strength.
Hear the concise affirmation of valor.
Read recognition of believing women in the source’s own terms.
shortened: Every maidservant who hath believed is regarded by God as amongst the most exalted of men.

order.why: Keep the related language of being counted among the chosen.
Consider the image of the rent veil and recognition.
Read steadfast courage alongside the source’s polemical comparison.
Keep the comparison centered on belief rather than biological sex.
shortened: Know thou that every woman who hath believed in God and purified her soul is better than a thousand men who have disbelieved in God and were remote from the paradise of nearness.

order.why: Read the reversal of learned men and recognizing women.
shortened: I swear by the Sun of the horizon of proof that handmaidens who today have attained unto the recognition of God, exalted be His glory, are and have been superior and more exalted in the sight of God than the men of the earth, be they divines or others.

order.why: Keep the companion contrast concerning access to utterance.
shortened: How many men who counted themselves among the most learned of the learned were seen to be deprived and forbidden from the choice wine and from the Kawthar of the utterance of the Self-Subsisting Lord, while the handmaidens of God attained thereunto.

order.why: Consider pride and recognition in the contrast between servants and handmaidens.
shortened: And at the end of the Tablet We make mention of My handmaidens who have believed in the One, the All-Informed. How many a servant hath been kept back through pride from the Lord of Revelation, and how many a handmaiden hath turned unto the Much-frequented Fane and believed in God, the Lord of all worlds. He giveth whom He willeth whatsoever He desireth. He, verily, is the Single One, the One Alone, the Mighty, the Powerful. Blessed is the handmaiden who hath attained unto My days, and turned unto My horizon, and clung to My luminous hem.

order.why: Read the invitation to gratitude for recognition.
shortened: O handmaidens of God! Render thanks and be engaged in His praise and glorification, inasmuch as He hath assisted you to attain a station whereof the men of earth, be they divines or others, remain deprived and debarred.

order.why: Keep love and heedlessness as the grounds of this comparison.
Hear the thanksgiving for women who turned toward revelation.
Read the emphatic promise about guidance and understanding.
Follow it with the clarification that particular women surpass particular men.
shortened: The expression which you quote, "Every woman who is directed to the guidance of God in this great age, will surpass men in every respect," signified that, in this age, certain women will appear who will surpass some men.

order.why: Consider the comparison with developed men of previous centuries.
shortened: Know in the reality of assurance that every true woman who is attracted by the fragrances of holiness in this most glorious age will surpass even the most developed men of previous centuries.

order.why: Read the warning that power may be directed toward differing ends.
shortened: O assured leaf! When thou observest the world events and the news and history of centuries, dispensations and ages, thou realisest that the greatest happenings and effects have been revealed and manifested from the female sex. But some have been the manifestations of glorious signs and some captives of the vainglory of lust and passion. Some became the cause of everlasting life to the world and its inhabitants, and others the cause of perpetual death of the unfortunate ones.

order.why: Consider the passage’s account of a former limitation removed.
shortened: O handmaiden of God! In former cycles, so numerous were the women who arose to serve and wandered in the wilderness of the love of God, yet they were not numbered as equal to men, inasmuch as it was unequivocally stated: "Men have superiority over women." Now, in this wondrous Revelation, women have indeed surpassed men, and this limitation hath been removed.

order.why: Read endeavor as the basis of advancement.
shortened: O thou leaf who art well assured! In this divine Dispensation, and in this heavenly Age, mankind has become freed from the shackles of the distinction between the feminine and the masculine. The one who exerteth the utmost endeavor, is the one who advanceth and excelleth. How numerous are the men who remained behind [the veil], and how many the women who became the heroines of the field.

order.why: Consider the account of courage and powerful utterance.
Keep the image of advancing in spiritual attainment.
Read the promise of participation in divine favors.
shortened: O handmaiden of God, O assured leaf! In this wondrous Dispensation, such a bounty has been bestowed upon women by the Abha Beauty, may my spirit be sacrificed for His loved ones, that it cannot be imagined. In truth, they have attained the station of men and have become the recipients of the favors of His Holiness the One in all matters.

order.why: Hear the particular assurance addressed to one woman.
shortened: O handmaiden of God! Praise the Divine Unity Who guided thee to the fountain of life and directed thee to the path of salvation, Who gave thee to drink from the Kawthar of inner meanings and sustained thee with heavenly sustenance, Who lit the candle of recognition in the glass of thy heart and illumined the lamp of guidance in the niche of thy mind.
Although thou wert among women, He made thee the pride of men and granted thee all manner of wishes.

order.why: Consider women as lights, mountains, and oceans of meaning.
shortened: O leaf of the Divine Tree! One of the manifest signs of the Day of God is that some women are raised from the slumber of self and heedlessness and gathered under the shadow of the banner of the all-embracing Word, who have become the glory of men and the light of the world. They have engaged the tongue in remembering the All-Merciful, and have refreshed the soul and existence with the fragrances of the Beloved. They have been steadfast as the immovable mountain in the Cause of God, and have scattered, as the surging sea, the pearls of meaning of divine knowledge.

order.why: Read conquest of hearts through knowledge and proof.
Join eloquence with a radiant conscience.
shortened: What favor and tender mercy this is, such priceless bounty and grace.

Praised be the Self-Subsisting Lord, Who through the recognition of His Faith caused women to become the pride of all men, and through the power of faith led them to triumph over the fearless warriors of the field. He endowed her with an eloquent speech, conferred upon her a mighty utterance, and bestowed on her an enlightened heart and an inspired soul. He granted her a life filled with tidings of joy, and bestowed upon her a crystal pure and radiant conscience.

order.why: Consider the diversity of capacities and expressions among women.
Read entry into the arena of knowledge and assurance.
shortened: The sphere of divine knowledge was thus far the arena of the masculine sex and the field of men, but in this glorious Cycle some women have been raised who have become the champions in the field of certitude, and dauntless in the arena of assurance.

order.why: Hear encouragement through the example of women in Persia.
shortened: Wonder not that thou hast attained to this great bounty, for in Persia some women were raised up who were flames of guidance and became the means of guiding many of the chosen ones.

order.why: Read the expectation of further development.
shortened: In this cycle, the world of women is in tumult and commotion from the outpourings of the Abha Beauty, and intoxicated and bewildered from the wine of favors. Day by day they are advancing. Soon you will observe that among women, souls will arise so attracted that they will cause amazement. They will become brilliant lamps and speakers of the proofs and evidences of the Lord of Bounties.

order.why: Consider the amazement associated with newly revealed capacities.
Read the enduring foundation laid through women’s service.
Keep the reported observation about boldness in faith.
Read the address’s sequence from deprivation toward strength and wisdom.
shortened: Whereas in the former time they were oppressed, now they have attained the greatest station of honor. Whereas formerly they were disappointed, now they are hopeful. While in the past they were deprived, praise be to God, they have taken a goodly portion; having been weak, praise be to God they have become strong; having been ignorant, praise be to God they have become wise. Whereas in the past they were considered inferior to men, now, through the Divine favors, they have superseded them in all the degrees of existence.

order.why: Consider gratitude expressed through an enkindled life.
shortened: Women have become verses of guidance and manifestations of the favors of the Most Glorious Beauty. In gratitude for this bounty, they must become so enkindled with the fire of the love of God as to prove they were deserving of these favors.

order.why: Read the hope that women will arise to promote the Cause.
Hear the call to raise the banner of recognition.
shortened: May the handmaidens of the merciful blaze with the fire of the love of God and raise aloft the banner of divine recognition.

order.why: Join an exalted station with counsel, deeds, and character.
Read service through trust, steadfastness, and sanctification.
shortened: Today, the service of the handmaidens of God hath been and is trust in God, steadfastness, and sanctification from that which is unseemly.

order.why: Hear the invitation to turn toward the horizon and receive bounty.
Keep the blessing on the recipient, her mother, and recognizing women.
Read recognition as honor and nearness.
shortened: O my handmaiden! Today each of the handmaidens of the earth has attained the most great honor and supreme bounty, which is the recognition of God, exalted be His glory. She is mentioned before God as being among the people of the most exalted Paradise and is recorded in the Book as one of the sincere ones and those brought nigh.

order.why: Consider the devotional meaning of being called a handmaiden.
Read the glad tidings for steadfast remembrance.
shortened: This is a Book which speaks with truth and gives glad tidings to those handmaidens who have believed in God their Lord, who were among those who stood firm on the Day of Resurrection, who remembered their Lord in the morning and evening, and who were among those who abide eternally in the pavilion of holiness.

order.why: Hear the hope that all the handmaidens share in purification and favor.
shortened: It is my hope that through the bounty of God His handmaidens may all without exception become adorned with such wondrous garment s as these and such beauteous robes so that each one of them may hear from the kingdom of holiness the words, "Verily God has purified thee and chosen thee amongst the women of the world."

order.why: Consider the warning about longing that does not become recognition.
Keep divine care beside the account of missed recognition.
shortened: The favors of God and His watchful care have ever been and shall continue to be directed toward His handmaidens. Consider this bounty as great and magnificent, for how many were the handmaidens of God who yearned for His days and ardently desired His presence, yet when He rent asunder the veil, they failed to recognize Him and partook not a drop from the cup of His love.

order.why: Read the summons to all and the limited response.
Consider devotion that is not prevented by attachment to kin.
shortened: Blessed art thou, doubly blessed art thou! Thou art reckoned amongst those handmaidens whose love for their kin hath not prevented them from attaining the shores of the Sea of Grace and Mercy.

order.why: Read hope for blame and censure to change into gratitude.
shortened: At every moment render thanks unto the Blessed Beauty for having conferred such bounty, of being subject to blame and severe censure, and to be exposed to the misdeeds of the people of error. This is the all-highest bounty; it is the outpourings of supreme mercy, and a token of the favor of the Abha Beauty. Ere long, blame will be transformed into thankfulness, and censure will change into praise and gratitude; and the handmaidens of God will each burn brightly even as a candle in the assemblies of women, and will beam forth as a star upon the horizon of eternal glory.

order.why: Hear the reported image of sacrifice becoming guidance.
Distinguish spiritual service from the passing sovereignty of empresses.
Read enduring influence amid poverty and oppression.
shortened: In the world of existence, there are no greater women than the queens of empires. Materially they have reached the highest station of womanhood and gained great riches, infinite power and glory. Notwithstanding all these advantages when they die and go under the earth, they disappear and become non-existent. They leave behind no name, no trace, no fruit and no sign. But the maid servants of God who are outwardly in the utmost poverty and imprisoned by the people of oppression, humiliated and scoffed at by the outsiders, ere long, they will crown their heads with the diadem of the everlasting Glory and [be] established upon the eternal throne of majesty.

order.why: Keep the contrast between earthly palaces and lasting honor.
shortened: O ye cherished handmaidens at the threshold of the Lord!

The ladies of the world will ultimately be brought low, and the queens of the earth will in the end be humbled and abased. Their flourishing palaces will become buried tombs, and their glory and grandeur will vanish and disappear. But the handmaidens of the Blessed Beauty will become the cherished ones of the heaven of paradise and the queens of the gardens of heaven.

order.why: Hear the concise comparison with queens.
shortened: I swear by the Sun of the horizon of inner meanings that these handmaidens are and have been greater and more exalted than the queens of the earth.

order.why: Consider the image of the true Layla.
Read hearts becoming gardens in spring.
Receive the greeting to women who have believed.
Keep the second greeting in its separate source wording.
shortened: From this station We send Our greetings upon the faces of My maidservants who have believed in God, the Powerful, the Exalted, the Mighty, the Wise.

order.why: Consider the care expressed in replying despite sorrow.
Close the linked readings with a blessing.
shortened: And the Spirit be upon thee and upon those women who have believed in God and were among those who attained.

order.why: Read love and faithfulness through the imagery of birds and dawn.
shortened: Glory be to Him Who maketh mention of His handmaidens who have believed in Him, who have detached themselves from all that is repugnant to His good-pleasure, who have walked in the ways of the righteous, and have hearkened unto the melodies of the birds of eternity from the direction of the Throne of God, the Most High, the Most Exalted, and who soar on the wings of love and faithfulness toward the most sublime and resplendent heaven at dawn and in the early hours.

order.why: Conclude with the supplied vision of love and service gaining weight in civilization.

questions: How does the image of humanity’s two wings change the way women’s advancement is understood?
What connections do these passages draw between education at home, intellectual development, and participation in public life?
How do particular women’s examples challenge assumptions about who may teach, lead, or speak with authority?
What does Priscilla and Aquila’s work with Apollos suggest about shared learning and the recognition of insight?
How might readers distinguish historical idioms and circumstances from the qualities and responsibilities the passages commend?
What could a community do to make fuller room for women’s knowledge, courage, and service?

references.label: 1 · Acts 18:24–26 · Priscilla, Aquila, and shared learning
references.note: Read how Priscilla and Aquila help Apollos, already an eloquent and learned speaker, understand the way of God more fully. Compare their shared teaching with this compilation’s accounts of women’s learning and spiritual leadership. What makes a community able to recognize insight across established expectations?

subjects.displayTitle: Equality of women and men: the flight of a shared humanity
subjects.introduction: A bird with one strong wing and one weak wing cannot rise, however hard it beats the air. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá returns to that image again and again, and it changes the question of equality from a matter of fairness between two parties into a matter of whether humanity as a whole can fly at all. Beneath the image lies a claim about human nature: women and men alike bear the divine image, and in the sight of God the only distinction between them is purity of heart and nobility of deed. From that root grow practical demands, for equal education, for rights and opportunity, for partnership in marriage rather than mastery, for women’s voice in the councils that decide between war and peace. The Qur’an’s verse naming women and men together in faith, patience, charity and remembrance [1] shows how old this pairing is in scripture. The journey continues toward the station and role of women in the new age, and toward the wider ordering of Bahá’í principles in which equality stands beside peace, education and the end of prejudice.
subjects.arc: Begin with interdependent progress, explore the spiritual basis of equality, follow education into rights and public participation, consider historical settings and institutional distinctions, and conclude with partnership and peace.

order.why: Open with the two wings and their shared flight.
Ground equality in the manifestation of divine names and attributes.
shortened: Know thou, O handmaid, that in the sight of Baha, women are accounted the same as men, and God hath created all humankind in His own image, and after His own likeness. That is, men and women alike are the revealers of His names and attributes, and from the spiritual viewpoint there is no difference between them. Whosoever draweth nearer to God, that one is the most favored, whether man or woman. How many a handmaid, ardent and devoted, hath, within the sheltering shade of Baha, proved superior to the men, and surpassed the famous of the earth.

order.why: Read the same effulgence shining upon women and men.
Connect rights and opportunity with the rejection of supposed innate deficiency.
shortened: It has been objected by some that woman is not equally capable with man and that she is deficient by creation. This is pure imagination. The difference in capability between man and woman is due entirely to opportunity and education.
The purpose, in brief, is this: that if woman be fully educated and granted her rights, she will attain the capacity for wonderful accomplishments and prove herself the equal of man.

order.why: Consider how limits imposed on women also limit men.
Read inequality as a source of discord.
Bring the principle into marriage as partnership.
Hear the removal of distinctions in the Supreme Pen’s language.
shortened: The Supreme Pen has removed the distinctions between servants and handmaidens, and through perfect grace and all-embracing mercy has established all upon a single plane.
In this Day the Hand of divine grace hath removed all distinctions. The servants of God and His handmaidens are regarded on the same plane.

order.why: Read equal respect beside differences of love and conduct.
Consider bounty embracing different circumstances and capacities.
Keep the concise affirmation of a common plane.
Read the related declaration of an equal station.
shortened: O handmaiden of God! The favours of the Kingdom are boundless and limitless, and they are beyond question and vain imagination. Therefore, male and female are one and the same, and men and bridal handmaidens enjoy an equal station. The one who advances more is nearer, and whoever is further enthused, is closer.

order.why: Hear the reported affirmation concerning the Kingdom.
Consider justice and equity without preference.
Read the radiance of faith across sex.
Explore divine image and likeness as a general human reality.
shortened: In the Torah it is written that God said, "Let us create man in Our image, after Our likeness," and in a tradition of the Prophet Muhammad it is stated: "God created Adam in His image." The meaning of this image is the divine image, that is, man reflects the attributes of God and manifests the qualities of the Lord.

Thus, man is a sign of the All-Merciful, created in the divine image and likeness. This applies generally and is not specific to men excluding women, for in God's sight there is no male and female. Whoever is more perfect is nearer to God, be it man or woman.

order.why: Keep the companion affirmation that all humanity bears the image.
Read knowledge, kindness, and purity as measures of nearness.
Consider good deeds and a pure heart in place of sex as a measure.
Read the source’s natural analogies alongside education and peace.
shortened: In the vegetable and animal kingdoms sex exists in perfect equality and without distinction or invidious estimate. The animal, although inferior to man in intelligence and reason, recognizes sex equality. Why should man, who is endowed with the sense of justice and sensibilities of conscience, be willing that one of the members of the human family should be rated and considered as subordinate?

In past ages humanity has been defective and inefficient because it has been incomplete. War and its ravages have blighted the world; the education of woman will be a mighty step toward its abolition and ending, for she will use her whole influence against war.

order.why: Consider the capacity to receive virtues and bestowals.
Read shared faculties and bounty within the human family.
Join faith with humanitarian action.
Question distinctions attributed to human choice rather than divine creation.
shortened: Another teaching is that there shall be perfect equality between men and women. Why should man create a distinction which God does not recognize?

order.why: Hear the concise appeal to common human origins.
Consider the source’s reversal of social loftiness and lowliness.
shortened: This is the Day whereon the distinctions of loftiness and lowliness have been abolished. Any soul, whether male or female, who hath turned unto the True One is reckoned as being of the True One, and apart from that is mentioned before the All-Merciful as being among the lost, even if they were of the most exalted in creation.

order.why: Read the ascendancy of spiritual qualities and the call to peace and fellowship.
Examine masculine and feminine terms as metaphor in this text.
shortened: O dust at the threshold of grandeur! Masculinity and femininity pertain to the soul, not to the body - to the heart, not to clay. For these two physical attributes are metaphorical, while their spiritual reality is truth. For we observe that a male person with an elephant-like physique can be as lowly, contemptible and weak as an ant, while behind the veil of chastity and purity, a female can be the epitome of strength and power - the former enslaved by self and passion, the latter noble through reason and restraint; the former sinful and the latter virtuous. Thus it becomes clear and evident that manliness and wisdom belong to the heart, not to water and clay.

order.why: Keep the source’s concise gendered idiom in that interpretive setting.
shortened: Today the handmaidens of God are accounted as men. Blessed are they and joy be unto them!

order.why: Read the companion statement without imposing a new meaning upon it.
Consider the contrast honoring steadfast handmaidens.
Read the crown image beside the common plane.
shortened: O handmaiden of God! In this precious age, the century of the mighty and omnipotent Lord, women have placed the crown of men upon their heads, inasmuch as all are gathered on the same plane.

order.why: Consider equality itself as a new garment and diadem.
shortened: O ye beloved maid-servants of God! In this most wonderful Dispensation God hath clothed the women with a new garment and hath crowned their heads with a glorious diadem - and that is equality between men and women.

order.why: Read the reported arguments about justice, faculties, and opportunity.
shortened: The other class, now representing the minority, but which ere long may become the majority, is of the opinion that perfect equality already exists. Those who are of this minority declare, first, that God is just, and justice demands an equal distribution of good gifts. They reason logically that it would be tyranny for God to show partiality, and the Lord is free from tyranny. They declare, secondly, that both man and woman being human all faculties and powers should be shared in common; that since creationally one sex has not been shown preference over the other we should not make a distinction that God has not created.

It must be admitted that in the past woman has not had the same educational opportunities that man has received, but when she is given equal advantages undoubtedly she will become his peer in knowledge and attainments.

order.why: Connect unequal opportunity with estimates of inferiority.
shortened: In proclaiming the oneness of mankind He taught that men and women are equal in the sight of God and that there is no distinction to be made between them. The only difference between them now is due to lack of education and training. If woman is given equal opportunity of education, distinction and estimate of inferiority will disappear. The world of humanity has two wings, as it were: One is the female; the other is the male. If one wing be defective, the strong perfect wing will not be capable of flight.

order.why: Read equal education and rights together.
Consider the equal obligation to educate girls and boys.
shortened: Girls are like boys - there is absolutely no difference. Ignorance in both is blameworthy, and lack of education in both types is repugnant. "Are those who know equal with those who know not?" This command is binding for both groups. In fact, if viewed with true insight, the education and training of girls is more necessary than boys, for these daughters will one day become mothers and nurturers of children.

order.why: Read a shared course of study as contributing to unity.
Join education with equal regard.
shortened: But the children of men are in need of education and civilization, and they require to be polished, till they become bright and shining. Man and woman both should be educated equally and equally regarded.

order.why: Keep the concise call for equal educational opportunity.
Read the same education and privileges as a brother.
Consider women’s education in relation to children’s spiritual development.
shortened: The education of women is more important than the education of men, because when women are educated, children also develop in spiritual life.

order.why: Keep the reported argument for prioritizing girls’ education.
Follow education toward occupations and accomplishment.
Read rights as enabling the acquisition of perfections.
Keep the natural analogies attributed while following its argument about opportunity.
shortened: Sex is not particularized to humanity; it exists throughout the animate kingdoms but without distinction or preference. In the vegetable kingdom there is complete equality between male and female of species. Likewise, in the animal plane equality exists; all are under the protection of God.

Woman's lack of progress and proficiency has been due to her need of equal education and opportunity. Had she been allowed this equality, there is no doubt she would be the counterpart of man in ability and capacity. The happiness of mankind will be realized when women and men coordinate and advance equally, for each is the complement and helpmeet of the other.

order.why: Distinguish equality affirmed as a principle from capacities becoming manifest in practice.
shortened: The realities of things have been revealed in this radiant century, and that which is true must come to the surface. Among these realities is the principle of the equality of man and woman -- equal rights and prerogatives in all things appertaining to humanity. Baha'u'llah declared this reality over fifty years ago. But while this principle of equality is true, it is likewise true that woman must prove her capacity and aptitude, must show forth the evidences of equality. She must become proficient in the arts and sciences and prove by her accomplishments that her abilities and powers have merely been latent.

order.why: Read the recognition that respected women still lacked fully realized rights.
shortened: In Europe and America, women are truly respected but their legitimate rights have not yet reached the degree of perfection, for their education in sciences and arts is not yet complete, and so forth from the divine teachings which are truly the life of the world and humanity today.

order.why: Consider the emphasis on acquiring sciences, virtues, and demonstrated capacities.
shortened: You must strive greatly, endeavor in acquiring sciences, exert effort in comprehending the realities of things, and devote boundless energy to human virtues. Know that divine grace encompasses you.

Women will progress when men themselves testify that women are equal to them. There is no need for struggle and contention. After children in school strive and acquire sciences and reach the utmost degree of perfection, everyone testifies that they are perfect - their very deeds testify to their perfection.

order.why: Read learning and argument as preparation for public contribution.
Consider women’s achievements as evidence of spiritual empowerment.
shortened: In this wondrous Dispensation, the favors of the Glorious Lord encompass the handmaidens of the All-Merciful, therefore they must, like men, snatch the ball from the field so it may be proven and established that the penetrating power of the Word of God in this new cycle has made women equal to men, and in the field of tests they seize the ball from the arena.

order.why: Read the particular recognition of women’s teaching work.
shortened: Most lovingly convey on behalf of `Abdu'l-Baha, the warmest Abha greetings to all the maidservants of God, and say that in this Dispensation, women have assumed the same position as men, nay rather in Europe and America they have even surpassed men in the teaching work as well as in their attraction to the Divine fragrances.

order.why: Keep the concise account of women teachers in America.
Read the companion description of lectures and reasoned proofs.
Consider the possibilities opened by women’s organized advancement.
shortened: Without doubt, women's groups are advancing in this age and striving to become equal with men. This is a great intention. If women's groups progress and gain power, they will accomplish many things they are currently unable to do.

order.why: Read the movement from seclusion into knowledge.
shortened: O handmaidens of the Court of Unity! The light of truth in this mighty Dispensation has cast its rays upon all, making no distinction between male and female. Women have attained the station of men, and those who were secluded have hastened to the arena of knowledge.

order.why: Consider recognition, certitude, and eloquence in the account of achievement.
Hear the promise of further entry into public activity.
shortened: O handmaid of God! Glad tidings! For in this divine Cycle women will soon gallop in the arena of men. In America, the clamor of the handmaids of the All-Merciful has shaken the very foundations. Behold what is happening!

order.why: Read endeavor as the ground of advancement.
shortened: O thou leaf who art well assured! In this divine Dispensation, and in this heavenly Age, mankind has become freed from the shackles of the distinction between the feminine and the masculine. The one who exerteth the utmost endeavor, is the one who advanceth and excelleth. How numerous are the men who remained behind [the veil], and how many the women who became the heroines of the field.

order.why: Keep the polo and heroism imagery focused on service.
shortened: Now, in this wondrous Revelation, women have indeed surpassed men, and this limitation hath been removed. All have been accounted with the same station. Whosoever ariseth further, shall obtain a greater share; and the valiant hero who urgeth ahead and hit the polo ball of service, will carry off the prize, and it maketh no difference whether man or woman, whether male or female. The Lord hath exalted the veiled woman above the men, she hath triumphed over the largest of armies, and hath won the leading prize in the fields of ecstasy and delight.

order.why: Consider the comparison with Rustam in its literary setting.
shortened: O pure leaf, throughout the dispensations men were the heroes of the battlefield and the valiant members of the army of revolt, but in this great cycle some women will arise who will become the envy of men, and the example to be emulated by the traditional hero, Rustam.

order.why: Read dignity through the metaphor of a new garment.
Keep the comparison with men in the West as a contextual statement.
shortened: In this cycle females have the station of males, rather in the West women have achieved superiority over men.

order.why: Read the particular assurance addressed to two women.
shortened: O ye two cherished handmaidens of the Abha Beauty! Although in ancient times the status of women was inferior compared to men, in this glorious Dispensation women are equal to men. Indeed, some of the handmaidens of the All-Merciful have outstripped men in the arena.

order.why: Distinguish circumstances in Persia from the reported equality of the Kingdom.
Read reported generalizations about gifts alongside its final measure of nearness to God.
Consider the reported shift from force toward love, service, and fuller balance.
shortened: The world in the past has been ruled by force, and man has dominated over woman by reason of his more forceful and aggressive qualities both of body and mind. But the balance is already shifting; force is losing its dominance, and mental alertness, intuition, and the spiritual qualities of love and service, in which woman is strong, are gaining ascendancy. Hence the new age will be an age less masculine and more permeated with the feminine ideals, or, to speak more exactly, will be an age in which the masculine and feminine elements of civilization will be more evenly balanced.

order.why: Read the full exchange, keeping the visitor’s answers distinct from the speaker’s words.
Retain the reporter’s question and the answer about rights and education.
shortened: Question: I have heard that you teach equality of rights between men and women.

Answer: The equality of rights between men and women is better established in America than elsewhere, and is advancing day by day. However, until complete equality between male and female is achieved in rights, the world of humanity will not make extraordinary progress. Women constitute one important pillar of two mighty pillars and are humanity's first teachers and educators, for mothers are the first teachers of young children. They establish moral character and educate children, who later study in higher schools. Now if the teacher and educator is deficient, how can the one educated become perfect? Therefore, the progress of women brings about the progress of men, hence women must be given complete education so they may reach the level of men.

order.why: Read the two wings in an address to the Women’s Freedom League.
shortened: Humanity is like a bird with its two wings -- the one is male, the other female. Unless both wings are strong and impelled by some common force, the bird cannot fly heavenwards. According to the spirit of this age, women must advance and fulfill their mission in all departments of life, becoming equal to men. They must be on the same level as men and enjoy equal rights. This is my earnest prayer and it is one of the fundamental principles of Baha'u'llah.

order.why: Consider equality as necessary to social and political progress.
shortened: And let it be known once more that until woman and man recognize and realize equality, social and political progress here or anywhere will not be possible. For the world of humanity consists of two parts or members: one is woman; the other is man. Until these two members are equal in strength, the oneness of humanity cannot be established, and the happiness and felicity of mankind will not be a reality.

order.why: Read women’s participation as essential to considering all sides of public questions.
shortened: In all questions which concern the welfare of a nation, is not the woman's view as important as the man's, if one would get a just and true consideration of all sides of that question? Therefore I am in favour of votes for women on every subject.

order.why: Keep the reported suffrage milestones in their historical setting.
Hear the expectation that equal rights will be realized.
Read the reported humorous reversal concerning which sex should demand equality.
Consider the two wings alongside the declaration of political detachment.
shortened: Regarding women's suffrage, this is a political issue and I am detached from all political matters, however I will say this much: both men and women are human and are like two wings for the world of humanity. If either of these wings is weak, the bird cannot fly. If both wings are strong, humanity will soar to the highest heaven.

order.why: Read the discussion of participation, voting, military exemption, and the House of Justice in full.
Keep the brief acknowledgment of exceptions.
Read the source’s categorical affirmation alongside its qualification.
shortened: Equality of men and women, except in some negligible instances, has been fully and categorically announced. Distinctions have been utterly removed.

order.why: Retain the related qualification in its own wording.
Read the reported question and answer on institutional membership as a distinct source.
Consider women’s membership in a meeting for the Temple.
Read a shared table as an enacted sign of equality.
shortened: In the olden time, it was not possible for women to sit at table in equality with the men, but in this Day it is different, and the change has been largely brought about by the position given to women in free America. It is the power of Baha'u'llah that made it possible for these American women to sit at this Table with these pilgrims. This is to show that in the Kingdom of Abha there will be equality established between women and men. They are equal.

order.why: Keep the account of meeting together across a former social barrier.
shortened: In the East it was prohibited for men and women to assemble in the same room. However in this Dispensation, the women have the same rank as men, and there is not the least difference between the two.

order.why: Read unity within the partnership of marriage.
Consider sympathy and friendship, retaining the report’s omissions.
Read the source’s connection between women’s influence and preventing war.
Connect equality with peace and the removal of prejudice.
Place equal rights within the teachings’ account of the world’s life.
shortened: Yet another of the teachings of Baha'u'llah is the equality of men and women and their equal sharing in all rights. And there are many similar principles. It hath now become evident that these teachings are the very life and soul of the world.

order.why: Read equality among a wider enumeration of principles.
Consider the connection with economic welfare and spiritual civilization.
Keep equality beside reason, peace, and the critique of prejudice.
Read the brief connection with economic principles.
shortened: They establish the equality of both sexes and propound economic principles which are for the happiness of individuals.

order.why: Join unity between women and men with equality of rights.
shortened: Seventh, unity between men and women and equality of rights.

order.why: Retain the concise enumeration.
shortened: Sixth is equality between men and women, and so forth.

order.why: Keep the separately reported enumeration in its source wording.
Return to the bird’s two wings and prosperity.
Read the brief companion image of strengthened wings.
Keep the interview’s formulation of the same relationship.
Read the reported question about access to life’s fullest opportunities.
Consider religion’s relationship to unequal privileges.
shortened: In the sight of the Heavenly Father all are equal. The religion of God is for the equalization of rights and not for the gradation of classes and the distribution of privileges. The religion of God is the leveller of all social inequalities and the destroyer of sacerdotal distinctions.

order.why: Keep the source’s comparative claim about earlier religions attributed to this address.
Read the report’s historical priority claim in its own setting.
Consider the reported response when the principle was proclaimed.
Read the historical account of denied education and public voice.
shortened: Women used to be oppressed in the Orient. They were in every respect humiliated. They were deprived of the opportunity to gain knowledge. They could not study science or art, and in politics they had no voice at all. Men did not consider them their equal. Baha'u'llah announced that women have the same right as men. He uplifted their conditions. He said, "The world of humanity has two wings, the one is man, the other woman."

order.why: Keep the broad account of former dispensations attributed to this report.
shortened: In all the former dispensations, men were considered superior to women. Women were lower than men; nay, rather during some of the past ages women were made captives of men. For example during the Mosaic dispensation women were captives of men, but in the dispensation of Baha'u'llah, His Bestowals have made men and women equal. He caused the people to put into active practice this social equality and declared that the women in this age shall make extraordinary advancement and they shall reach to such a degree, that no difference will be left between men and women.

order.why: Distinguish the reporter’s comparative framing from the quoted two-wings image.
Read the reported removal of distinctions.
Consider the source’s critique of practices that exceeded stated religious provisions.
shortened: Although in the Dispensation of the Furqan (Qur'an) women were considered the weaker sex and received few rights - "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women" was revealed and "To the male the equivalent of the portion of two females" was sent down - yet the people of the Furqan went beyond bounds and exceeded all limits, such that poor women became captives and like purchased slaves.

But praise be to God, in this divine Dispensation of justice such a pavilion and tent has been raised at the pole of the horizons that women have become equal sharers and partners with men in all rights, and they have raised the banner of "How many women kept in seclusion and behind veils have surpassed men!"

order.why: Keep its account of former and present dispensations in source context.
Hear the concise declaration concerning women’s freedom.
shortened: I am the founder and promoter of women's freedom.

order.why: Read emancipation as a pillar alongside counsel about manner of speech.
shortened: The emancipation of women is one of the pillars of the Cause of God; it is for this reason I sent the blessed leaf Ruha to Paris and London and the maidservants of God Zinat and Qudsiyyih to America, that they might become role models for the women of the East.

For the present, however, thy daughters must speak with moderation concerning the emancipation of women in Europe. They must not appear strident, for stridency bringeth about other harms. One's speech must be mild.

order.why: Consider the pursuit of rights through intellectual and spiritual development.
Read the reported counsel for prudent educational means.
Keep the warning about hostile opposition in its particular historical circumstances.
shortened: Regarding women's liberation, a detailed confidential letter was written to you. Now observe how it was the essence of wisdom, otherwise the followers of Yahya along with the Ja'fari committee and others would have raised the banner of corruption during Ramadan and Muharram, and their cries of woe would have reached the vault of heaven.

order.why: Read signs of the effect of earlier talks about rights.
shortened: The talks which were given about the 'rights of women', praise be to God, now their signs have appeared!

order.why: Hear the assurance of equality addressed to one woman.
Read the debate as reported, distinguishing the women’s quoted position.
Consider the scepter of equality as a final image of advancement.
Keep the narrator’s account of the address distinct from direct quotation.
Read the supplied institutional explanation and its rejection of male superiority.
Keep the supplied translation’s statement of spiritual equality.
Read the authorized supplied translation in its own wording and authority.
shortened: In former ages, men enjoyed ascendancy over women because bodily might reigned supreme and the spirit was subject to its dominion. In this radiant age, however, since the power of the spirit hath transcended that of the body and assumed its ascendancy, authority and dominion over the human world, this physical distinction hath ceased to be of consequence; and, as the sway and influence of the spirit have become apparent, women have come to be the full equals of men. Today, therefore, there is no respect or circumstance in which a person's sex provideth grounds for the exercise of either discrimination or favour.

order.why: Close with full partnership as a prerequisite of peace.

questions: What does the two-wings image reveal about the effects of unequal opportunity on everyone?
How do the passages connect spiritual equality with rights, education, and the practical conditions of daily life?
What is the difference between possessing capacities and having the opportunity to make them visible?
How does Qur’an 33:35’s repeated naming of women and men shape the reader’s understanding of moral agency?
How can the various historical conversations and institutional explanations be read together with care for their sources and contexts?
What habits and arrangements would need to change for fuller partnership to contribute to peace?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 33:35 · Women and men named together
references.note: Read the verse’s parallel naming of women and men in faith, truthfulness, perseverance, humility, charity, fasting, chastity, and remembrance. Both are promised forgiveness and reward. Compare this explicit moral and spiritual pairing with the compilation’s account of common spiritual capacities and its further discussion of education and public opportunity.

subjects.displayTitle: Beyond party conflict: service, impartiality, and public responsibility
subjects.introduction: Standing apart from party conflict is easy to mistake for indifference, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá will not allow the mistake. The friends who kept clear of every faction during Iran’s revolution were, in His account, well-wishers of all, busy with educating children, improving morals and reconciling government and people; serving nation and government was an obligation, while forming parties or rising against the ruling power was forbidden. That distinction between public responsibility and factional allegiance is the heart of the matter, with room for honest public employment, for voting in a republic, and for cooperation with anyone pursuing a constructive aim. It asks something harder than withdrawal: impartial goodwill toward people bitterly opposed to one another, and a refusal to become anyone’s instrument. First Peter’s joining of respect for rulers, honourable conduct and freedom exercised as servants of God describes the same posture. The path leads on into the constitutional revolution in Iran, where these instructions were first tested, into obedience to and respect for government authority, and into the protection of the Cause whose unity the whole practice exists to guard.
subjects.arc: Begin with constructive service and goodwill, distinguish public responsibility from factional allegiance, read the warnings in their historical settings, examine community practice, then consider later explanations and cooperation for shared aims.

order.why: Open with education, equality, peace, and the source’s critique of political intrigue.
Read goodwill without attachment to a party or resentment toward a group.
shortened: During the revolution in Iran, praise be to God, you were well-wishers of all and strove for universal peace and reconciliation. You had no attachment to any party nor any resentment toward any group.

order.why: Give service a concrete social horizon in Iran’s moral renewal.
Read the explicit distinction between political faction and service to nation and government.
Consider honest public employment within that distinction.
Read the particular guidance on participation in republican elections.
shortened: In the United States it is necessary that the citizens shall take part in elections. This is a necessary matter and no excuse from it is possible. My object in telling the believers that they should not interfere in the affairs of government is this: That they should not make any trouble and that they should not move against the opinion of the government, but obedience to the laws and the administration of the commonwealth is necessary. Now, as the government of America is a republican form of government, it is necessary that all the citizens shall take part in the elections of officers and take part in the affairs of the republic.

order.why: Distinguish official responsibilities from interference outside one’s duties.
Explore the account of religion’s contribution to morals and justice.
Consider a universal aim that benefits humanity.
shortened: And every conscientious aim, if it brings good to the human world, being universal, is a divine project. From prancing in the political arena, only a mere nest and dwelling will be arranged, but soaring in the divine atmosphere is ascending to the apex of glory.

order.why: Read abstention alongside character, compassion, and harmony.
Join impartiality with universal love.
Read composure and love in the counsel against sedition.
Consider reconciliation between government and people.
shortened: We have no connection with any party: we are neither partisans of the victorious Government nor do we share the opinions of the glorious people. We stand aside from all strifes, wish well to all, and offer our prayers and supplications at the Throne of God that He will reconcile these two honourable elements with one another, so that they may become one element, and may work together for the glory and advancement of both Government and people.

order.why: Place that reconciliation within the account of Iran’s revolution.
Read obedience, goodwill, and practical peace together.
shortened: They must act according to the instructions, which are that they should obey the government and be well-wishers to both sides and as much as possible be the cause of peace and tranquility, but absolutely not interfere in conflict and strife.

order.why: Consider efforts for harmony and the instruction to withdraw if powerless.
shortened: Therefore, O loved ones of God, strive so that complete harmony and unity may be achieved between the government and people, and if you remain powerless, withdraw completely.

order.why: Keep the concise companion instruction in that context.
Read the hope for national progress without warfare.
Ask about the relation between chosen means and hoped-for results.
Consider the wide field of justice, kindness, and service described here.
Read peace and goodwill as continuing commitments.
shortened: You must persist in peace, amity, love and goodwill toward all people, loyalty to the government, and non-interference in political affairs.

order.why: Join obedience with reconciliation across peoples and communities.
Consider truthfulness, love, and kindness in relations with everyone.
Keep sincere goodwill toward peoples and governments together.
shortened: They must be truthful and kind to all the peoples of the world, deal with all humanity with pure intent, absolute benevolence and heartfelt love, be sincere and well-wishing toward all the governments of the world, and, in accordance with Baha'u'llah's testament, never interfere in political matters - indeed, not even discuss them.

order.why: Read the concise joining of noninterference and kindness.
Consider humility and refusal to cause grief in this counsel.
shortened: Offend not the mind of any person and grieve not the heart of any man; be towards all with the utmost humility and meekness, and be loyal and sincere subjects to the Royal Throne; obey the authorities of affairs, and make no interference whatsoever with political matters; adorn the meetings with the commemoration of God and train the individuals with the breath of the merficul One; utter no word save in the mention of God, and rest only in the shadow of hope.

order.why: Read the call to give comfort and joy alongside the answer concerning government discussion.
shortened: The point is that the friends must not utter a word about political matters, for these do not concern them. Rather, they must occupy themselves with their own affairs and services, and nothing more. They must think only of drawing near to God, arising to serve His good-pleasure, and becoming the cause of comfort, ease, joy and gladness to the world of humanity. Should any person attempt to speak before the friends about governmental and state matters, saying that so-and-so said this or did that, the believer must respond: "These matters do not concern us.

order.why: Keep enlightenment and the correction of morals as the stated work.
Read the reported focus on hearts, education, and morals.
shortened: These papers are about politics. We do not interfere in the affairs of politics at all. We interfere in the affairs of the heart, in education and in morals.'

order.why: Read the source’s judgment about religious leaders intervening in politics.
Consider the distinction drawn between thought and external conditions.
Read unity and moral life as the stated focus.
Keep the distinction between the Kingdom and earthly sovereignty in the source’s terms.
shortened: And I say to you that this Cause absolutely has no involvement in politics, rather it is purely spiritual, related to the Kingdom rather than to earthly sovereignty and the material realm.

order.why: Consider divine politics as an image of all-embracing mercy.
Read the source’s comparison of political affairs with the Cause.
Hear the brief prayer contrasting divine and political orientations.
shortened: I beseech God to make you divine, not political.

order.why: Consider the warning against using religion as a party instrument.
Keep the reported limitation of political power as a unifying force.
Read the reported independence from political power.
